subject: Scope-based per-token structure for hosted API commit discussion
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@datacraft.ai>
Cc: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API proposal & commit bands — initial scope

Samir — great to meet earlier. As discussed, sketching a scope and a commit structure for DataCraft's expected hosted usage so your procurement team can review. High level:

- Estimated steady-state: ~1.2B tokens/month (inference) with seasonal peaks to ~1.8B.
- Preferred model family: LlamaX-13B variant (latency and quality tradeoff).
- Goal: usage-based billing with a 12-month commit.

Attached is a quick workbook with two pricing shapes: flat per-token breakpoints and a tiered per-token slab that increases discounts at larger commit bands. We're flagging two negotiation levers: effective per-token floor vs a committed monthly minimum.

Ask: Can you share the procurement timeline and whether you need an explicit SOW or if a PO + standard T&Cs will work?

Attachments: DataCraft_commit_proposal.xlsx

Thanks — happy to hop on a call with procurement next week.

—Ben
Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir@datacraft.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: DataCraft Procurement <procure@datacraft.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API proposal & commit bands — initial scope

Ben — thanks, this is helpful. Procurement asked for:

1) A clear, single per-token charge we can put on the PO (not multiple hidden fees).
2) Concurrency & latency SLAs for the LlamaX-13B endpoint (p50/p95).
3) A mechanism for overage protection during our peaks without surprise bills (either soft cap or pre-approved surge tiers).

We prefer a 12-month term with monthly committed spend rather than daily/variable commits. Their initial target: a committed monthly token floor equivalent to 1B tokens, with surge credits available for 50% above commit.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can give a named rate for 12-month 1B commit vs a pure rate-card reference? Procurement also asked whether a limited, one-time onboarding credit is possible for the first 90 days.

—Samir
CTO, DataCraft
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: DataCraft ask — named per-token rate vs rate card carveout?

Laura / team — forwarding Samir's asks. Quick summary and recommended internal path:

- Request: Named per-token rate for a 12-month commit with a 1B token/month floor and surge credits to cover up to 1.5B without immediate overage shock.
- Customer sensitivity: large logo, referenceable, likely to expand into dedicated in 9–12 months if latency profile holds.
- Revenue steer: modeled ARR ~ $X (see workbook) with 25–30% margin at the named rate if we also enable KV caching and conservative batching defaults.

Proposed commercial options (short list):
1) Rate-card + standard volume breakpoints (no special approval).
2) 7% off rate-card for the 1B commit band if legal signs standard T&C + annual prepay.
3) Custom slab: blended per-token rate of $0.0007 for first 1B, $0.00055 up to 1.5B, with a one-time onboarding credit of $15k. Requires pricing manager approval and VP sign-off.

Operational asks: Monica — can you confirm whether Named Rate + surge credits can be supported via our hosted routing policy without provisioning Dedicated? Also, what telemetry and routing SLOs would we promise for p95?

Ben — can you attach the workbook export you used and the modeled margin assumptions? I attached a pared-down fallback matrix (pricing_fallback_matrix.csv).

I recommend option 3 given the strategic fit; request: Laura, can you approve escalation to the pricing committee to grant the custom slab if necessary? If we can approve at your level (VP Sales) we can keep procurement moving.

—Rohan
Head of Enterprise Sales (acting)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 May 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: DataCraft ask — named per-token rate vs rate card carveout?

Thanks — read the matrix. Decision and conditional approval:

- Approve option 3 (custom slab) subject to two conditions:
  1) Legal to accept standard enterprise T&Cs with a mutual SLA addendum (we will not pre-accept non-standard indemnities).
  2) Finance sign-off on the $15k onboarding credit and expected margin at the blended rate (Monica, please loop in FP&A).

Implementation notes: pricing ops will create a named rate card entry for deal_id DC-2027-089; include an automatic fallback to rate-card pricing after the 12-month commit term. Surges: allow soft-cap bursts up to 50% above monthly commit with automatic notifications and an opt-out hard cap in the portal.

Ben — please reply to Samir with the named per-token offering and include a short bulleted mutual action plan (PO timing, SLA doc, onboarding credit terms, technical kickoff). Keep the language conditional "subject to legal & finance sign-off" to avoid commitment before sign-offs. Attach the workbook and the fallback matrix.

Laura
VP, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
